item.title: US urges citizens to take 'extreme caution' when using airports in Saudi Arabia
item.description:
US urges citizens to take 'extreme caution' when using airports in Saudi Arabia

The US State Department has urged their citizens to take "extreme caution" when travelling through airports in Saudi Arabia, amid renewed attacks.

Its official account on X said it is "aware" of additional attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

"U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization to use the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, as well as the airports in Jeddah and Dammam," the post read. 

"Please take extreme caution when using all major airports in Saudi Arabia. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions."

Saudi Arabia: The U.S. Mission is aware of additional attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a targeted attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on October 11. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization to use the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, as well as the airports in Jeddah and Dammam. Please take extreme caution when using all major airports in Saudi Arabia. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport. Private car, train, and bus options may provide alternatives to air travel. More at: https://t.co/H8o3ylZ2wg

item.title: Two Indian nationals missing after drone attack on tanker off Oman's coast
item.description:
Two Indian nationals missing after drone attack on tanker off Oman's coast

A drone attack on a vessel off the coast of Oman left two Indian nations missing, a senior Indian official said on Sunday.

Meanwhile, nine others were rescued, as search and rescue operations by the local coast guard begin.

"On Oct 11, tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was subjected to a drone attack at Sohar Anchorage," Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said in a post on X.

"While nine of our Indian crew members have been successfully rescued and are safe, two Indian nationals currently remain missing."

Sonowal added that India is "continuously coordinating with all relevant authorities to fully support the ongoing rescue efforts and ensure every possible action is taken to safely locate our missing personnel".

Since the war on Iran began in late February, at least 16 Indian seafarers have been killed.

item.title: Watch: Moment deadly Houthi strike hits Riyadh's King Khaled Airport
item.description:
Watch: Moment deadly Houthi strike hits Riyadh's King Khaled Airport

Footage obtained by Al Arabiya English shows the moment a Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport as passengers, including Umrah pilgrims, waited to board their flights.

The attack on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300, according to Saudi authorities. A further attack on Sunday caused a fire at the airport and injured several others. 

The strikes come amid escalating fighting in Yemen, Saudi Arabia has intensified its military campaign against Houthi forces in recent weeks, prompting threats of further attacks.

item.description:

  • Analysis: attack will force rethink of Trump strategy

A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday, the day after a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people.

An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport, starting a fire, killing one person and injuring 11, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. It was the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week.

item.title: How Low Can the Strategic Petroleum Reserve Actually Go?
item.description: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve held just 283 million barrels of oil at the end of September, according to Reuters, the lowest level since October 1982, back when the reserve was still being filled for the first time. It's a scary-looking number, and most of the coverage has treated it that way. But the barrel count is the easy part of this story. Oil came out of those Gulf Coast salt caverns fast, because that's exactly what the system was built to do. item.title: Middle East crisis: Riyadh airport hit again as Houthis claim attacks, including strike that killed 12 – as it happened
item.description:
This live blog is now closed. You can read our latest full report here:

  • Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say

Some more Gulf reaction to Houthi’s deadly airport attack and continued threats to target Saudi airspace.

In a significant message, the United Arab Emirates has issued a statement in solidarity with Saudi Arabia – expressing support for “all measures aimed at safeguarding the kingdom’s security and stability”.

The UAE message is improtant given the major rupture in relations this year between the two oil-rich kingdoms, first sparked by lingering divisions in Yemen, and made worse by the Iran War and arguments over oil prices which led to the UAE quitting OPEC (currently led by the Saudis) after six decades of membership.

Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.
